FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Doctor Visit flashcards.

A whole check-up, one calm card at a time. A teddy bear comes along on every step: the appointment, the waiting room, the doctor’s hello, the stethoscope’s listen, the deep breath — and the proud walk home. The cards run in visit order on purpose: the gentle steps first, and the two big ones (the x-ray, the hospital bed) arrive late, when your child already knows the story. Nothing at a check-up is a punishment, and medicine is only taken from a grown-up.

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page, and every card shows its age pill — start with the group that fits your child today.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Play doctor at home

    Let your child be the doctor and check their teddy with a toy stethoscope — ears, tummy, one deep breath. The child in the doctor’s seat is the child who stops worrying about the real one.

  2. 02

    Tell the visit in order

    Lay the cards out like a story: appointment first, goodbye last. Before a real appointment, walk the story once — "first we wait, then the doctor listens, then we go home." Knowing the order is the whole comfort.

  3. 03

    The medicine rule, said kindly

    Spread the cards and ask which one is the medicine. Then say the rule together, every time: medicine comes from a grown-up, only from a grown-up. The card says it too — same words, same rule.

  4. 04

    Pack the teddy

    Real check-ups go better with a familiar friend. Use the cards to "pack" for the visit — the teddy, the name-tag answer, the deep breath — and let your child carry the bag.

      Appointment Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Getting ready

      An appointment is the time you and the doctor agree on — the day your child’s check-up will happen, written on the calendar.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Appointment! A time to visit the doctor. Look — the calendar says TODAY. We get dressed, we take teddy, and off we go!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Circle the appointment on a real calendar and let your child cross off the days. A countdown turns a surprise into a plan — and plans are what calm little worries.

      Quick parent note

      Name the day and the who ("Tuesday, Dr. Ruiz") more than the why. Children handle check-ups well when the appointment is an ordinary, expected thing.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Reception Desk Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Getting ready

      The reception desk is the front desk of the clinic — the friendly person behind it says hello and tells the doctor you have arrived.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Reception desk! We tell the receptionist our name. "Hello, we are here!" She already knows — the doctor is expecting us.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play reception at home: a toy phone, a notebook, and your child behind the "desk" saying "hello, who is here today?" — with every stuffed animal checking in by name.

      Quick parent note

      The first two minutes of a visit are mostly waiting and saying hello. When children know the desk comes first, the whole arrival feels familiar.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Name Tag Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Getting ready

      A name tag says who your child is — the helpers at the clinic wear them too, so everyone knows everyone’s name.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Name tag! It helps people know your name. The doctor reads it: "Hello, Alex!" — and now you are friends.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Make a paper name tag together before a real visit — your child’s name, a drawing, maybe one for teddy. Wearing it in the waiting room is a small pride moment.

      Quick parent note

      A name tag makes a stranger into a helper with a name. Children who hear their own name spoken kindly settle faster almost every time.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Waiting Room Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Getting ready

      The waiting room is where families sit for a few minutes until it is their turn — a calm pause with chairs, maybe books, and teddy on a lap.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Waiting room! We wait for our turn. Teddy waits too. Soon a helper will call our name — and then the visit begins!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Keep a tiny "waiting bag": one small book or quiet toy that only comes out at the clinic. Waiting with a job is easy; waiting with nothing is long.

      Quick parent note

      Waiting is the hardest skill on this page. Two minutes of practice at home — a "waiting game" with a surprise at the end — pays off at the real clinic.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Doctor Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Meeting the helpers

      The doctor is the helper whose whole job is keeping your child healthy — and who kneels down to say hello before anything else.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Doctor! A doctor helps you feel better. She says hello, she asks teddy how he feels, and she takes gentle care of you.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Read the doctor card, then the Class 33 community-helpers cards: the doctor at the clinic, the dentist in the chair — helpers everywhere. Name them all.

      Quick parent note

      Children read faces fast. A doctor who says hello at child height is already halfway to a successful check-up — and so is a child who expects the hello.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Nurse Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Meeting the helpers

      The nurse is the helper who takes care of the small things — the height check, the questions, the gentle reassurance — before the doctor arrives.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Nurse! A nurse helps care for you. She knows all about bandages and kind words, and she shows the doctor how you are doing.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play nurse with the teddy hospital: the nurse takes teddy’s temperature, wraps his paw, and says "all better." Swap roles halfway through.

      Quick parent note

      Many children meet the nurse first — that first friendly face sets the tone. Giving the nurse a name at home ("Nurse Anna") makes the real one easier to greet.

      Teach it, step by step

      Weigh-In Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Meeting the helpers

      The weigh-in is standing on the little scale — it tells the doctor how much your child has grown since last time.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Weigh-in! Stand on the scale — click! The scale checks how much you weigh. You grew! Last time you were smaller!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Weigh the family, one by one, on the bathroom scale — including teddy. Numbers are just facts about bodies, and facts lose their scariness with practice.

      Quick parent note

      Growing is the headline of every check-up, and the scale is how the doctor sees it. A child who hears "you grew!" steps off that scale proud.

      Teach it, step by step

      Exam Room Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+Meeting the helpers

      The exam room is the doctor’s own room — the exam bed to sit on, the little sink, the poster on the wall, and teddy’s seat right beside.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Exam room! This is where check-ups happen. Sit on the big bed — boing! Teddy sits next to you. The doctor will be right in.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Arrange chairs and a couch cushion into an "exam room" for teddy. Every familiar prop at home removes one unknown at the clinic.

      Quick parent note

      The exam bed looks big and talks in crinkly paper. Naming it "the sitting bed" and letting a child climb on at home makes the real one just a place to sit.

      Teach it, step by step

      Check-Up Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      A check-up is the doctor looking and listening to make sure everything is growing the way it should — it is not a fix for anything being wrong.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Check-up! A check-up keeps you healthy. The doctor listens, looks and checks — and says "everything is growing just right!"”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Give the teddy a full check-up in order: ears, mouth, tummy, heart. Then swap — your child is the doctor, you are the patient who sits very still.

      Quick parent note

      The word itself matters: a check-UP, like a look-under-the-hood, not a repair. Children who hear "check" as "counting what is already good" sit easy.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Stethoscope Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      The stethoscope is the tool with the round listening end — the doctor wears it to hear the heart’s drum and the breath’s wind.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Stethoscope! A doctor listens to your heart. Boom-boom, boom-boom — that is YOUR heart, talking!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      A toy stethoscope (or a paper tube pressed to the chest) lets your child hear a real heartbeat — yours first, then teddy’s, then their own.

      Quick parent note

      The cold disc on the tummy startles nobody who has heard a heartbeat before. Play the listening game at home and the real thing becomes a treasure hunt: "there it is!"

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Thermometer Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      The thermometer is the little stick that measures how warm the body is — a quick tick that tells the doctor important things.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Thermometer! It checks your temperature. Tick-tock, a little beep — all done! The doctor reads the number.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Check the temperature of everything: teddy (warm!), your child’s forehead, the bath water with the bath thermometer. Measuring is a game bodies love.

      Quick parent note

      The word is long and wonderful — practice saying it: ther-MOM-e-ter. A child who can say the tool’s name owns the tool a little.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Ear Check Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      The ear check is the doctor looking inside the ear with a tiny flashlight — one second per ear, warm and gentle.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Ear check! The doctor looks inside your ear — a teeny light! Hold still like a statue… one… two… all done!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Play "what is in your ear?" with a flashlight at home — look in teddy’s ears, then your child’s (gently, never deep). Statues get prizes.

      Quick parent note

      A one-second light in the ear is nothing — unless you do not know it is coming. "A tiny light, one-two, done" is the whole script to rehearse.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Mouth Check Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      The mouth check is the doctor looking at the teeth and tongue — your child opens wide, says "aah," and the visit continues.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Mouth check! Open wide and say AHHH. The doctor sees your teeth and your tongue — what a big open mouth!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practice the "aah" in the mirror — the bigger the better, with a silly face at the end. Then check every stuffed animal’s mouth in the house.

      Quick parent note

      "Say ah" turns an inspection into a game every toddler already knows from tooth-brushing. Same mouth, same sound, different helper — easy transfer.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Eye Chart Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      The eye chart is the poster with letters and pictures on the wall — your child points the right way to show how well the eyes see.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Eye chart! We read letters and pictures with our eyes. Which way does the E point? You show it with your hands!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Make a home eye chart: a heart, a star, a cup drawn on paper — "which way is the heart pointing?" Pointing games are vision checks in disguise.

      Quick parent note

      Most three-year-olds cannot name letters but can point — the pictures on the chart exist exactly for them. Practice pointing left, right, up, down and the game is won.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Deep Breath Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+The check-up

      The deep breath is the doctor’s request during the listening part — breathe in like smelling a flower, out like blowing a candle.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Deep breath! Breathe in and out slowly. Smell the flower… blow the candle… again! The doctor is listening to your wind.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Practice flower-and-candle breathing anywhere — in the car, at bath time. It is a check-up skill AND the classic calm-down trick in one.

      Quick parent note

      A slow breath out is the most portable calming tool a child can own. Learning it for the doctor quietly hands them a lifelong skill.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      X-Ray Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5The check-up

      An x-ray is a special picture of the inside of the body — the bones show up white, and nothing about it hurts at all.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “X-ray! It takes a picture inside your body. Look — those are your BONES! The camera never touches you. Click, all done.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Look at hand x-rays together (a library book or a quick print) and find the finger bones. Wave at the picture — those bones wave back.

      Quick parent note

      The x-ray mostly stays a "maybe" card for a check-up — but naming it removes the mystery of the lead apron and the big machine in the hallway. A camera, nothing more.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Medicine Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+After the visit

      Medicine is what helps the body get better when it is sick — and the rule lives right on the card: it is taken only from a grown-up.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Medicine! Take it only from a grown-up. Grown-ups measure it, grown-ups give it — and then it helps your body do its healing work.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Say the rule together at every medicine moment — the same words, every time. And keep all real medicine up high, out of small hands and out of the game.

      Quick parent note

      This is the safety line of the whole set. Medicine is not candy and not a toy; children who hear the rule from birth never have to learn it the hard way.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Bandage Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+After the visit

      A bandage is the little soft sticker that covers a small cut — it keeps the spot clean while the body does its quiet healing.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Bandage! It helps a small cut heal. Clean it, stick it on — see? The bandage is the band-aid’s job, and your body does the rest.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Bandage a teddy’s scraped paw, then let your child wear one "just because." A bandage worn proudly stops being a sign something went wrong.

      Quick parent note

      The bandage is comfort as much as medicine. One on the teddy and one on the child is a perfectly sized first-aid kit for a three-year-old.

      Teach it, step by step

      Hand Washing Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+After the visit

      Hand washing is the soap-and-water habit that keeps germs from spreading — done here, done at school, done every day at home.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Hand washing! Clean hands help keep germs away. Soap, bubbles, scrub scrub, rinse — goodbye, germs!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Sing one whole alphabet song while washing — that is the famous twenty seconds. The clinic sink, the kitchen sink, the bathroom sink: germs lose everywhere.

      Quick parent note

      The visit ends the way good health starts: with soap. Washing hands before leaving the clinic is both a real habit and a perfectly calm way to close the day.

      Teach it, step by step

      Hospital Bed Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 4–5After the visit

      A hospital bed is a special bed that can go up and down with buttons — made so someone resting can be comfortable while they heal.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Hospital bed! A cozy bed helps you rest. It goes UP with a button — and down! Teddy tried it. If ever someone needs it, the bed is there.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Up-and-down is the magic: a recliner chair or a stack of pillows can "be" a hospital bed for teddy. Buttons and pillows — that is the whole wonder.

      Quick parent note

      Most check-up days never see this bed at all — it belongs here so it stays ordinary. "A cozy bed that helps you rest" is the whole idea a child needs.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      Feel Better Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+After the visit

      Feel better is the walk-home feeling: the visit is done, the stickers are earned, and the grown-up says the magic words — you did a great job.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Feel better! You did a great job at your check-up. You opened wide, you breathed deep, you were brave — and now, the walk home!”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Invent a check-up celebration: the same song or treat after every visit. A tradition turns "the doctor" into a story with a happy ending, every time.

      Quick parent note

      Ending on pride is the point of the whole set. Children remember the last five minutes longest — make them the walk-to-the-car high-five.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Doctor Visit (Extra Class) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · DOCTOR VISIT · AGES 3–5 YEARS

      Goodbye Flashcard for Preschoolers

      Ages 3+After the visit

      The goodbye is waving to the doctor at the door — the visit is finished, the next appointment is already an ordinary thing to look forward to.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Goodbye! The visit is finished. Wave to the doctor — "bye-bye, see you next time!" And home you go, hand in hand.”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Have the toys say goodbye after every teddy check-up — "bye-bye, Doctor!" Practiced goodbyes are easy goodbyes.

      Quick parent note

      A calm goodbye tells the child the story is complete. When the last card of the visit is a wave, the whole visit reads like a circle that closes gently.

      Teach it, step by step
